incident-bot: ALERT: cont-batch path p99 latency breach detected for production us-west-2 - service: text-generation - p95=120ms p99=2.8s (SLO: p99 < 1.5s). paging oncall rotation. automated mitigation: none applied.

Ava (oncall): reading dashboards — confirmed. streaming stall rate up ~4x on the cont-batch fast-path, tail queue length spiking on batcher-0/3.

Priya (sre): @Ava are customers impacted or just internal probe traffic? any recent deploys?

Ava (oncall): quick check: customer-facing 99th requests increased error/fallbacks: increase in stream disconnects and timeouts. No deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot.

Jules (backend): logs show a growing number of mega-seq requests hitting the continuous batching scheduler — mixed seqlen distribution is causing big batches to form then stall. snippet:

```
batcher-0 | enqueue req id=0x9a3 seq_len=5120 -> grouped with smalls
batcher-0 | kv-cache miss count rising
batcher-0 | schedule_delay=430ms, exec_wait=1.8s
```

Ben (infra): I see increased kernel scheduling delay on the GPU host (nvutil queue depth). Could be bursty multi-tenant load.

Maya (observability): metrics: batch_size_p50=8 p95=64 p99=128; tail_serialize_latency increased; streaming_ack_lag p99=2.3s. correlation: big batches with one long seq create padding amplification.

Ava (oncall): immediate mitigation ideas — (1) enforce seqlen bucketing / limit mixing (2) reduce max_batch_tokens on cont-batch path (3) enable preemptive scheduling to favor streaming requests (4) route streaming to the streaming-optimized variant. Thoughts?

Jules (backend): agree. We can flip `enable_seqlen_bucketing = true` for the cont-batch policy and set `bucket_threshold = 1024` to avoid grouping very long requests with short ones. Patch ready.

Ben (infra): for quick safety I'd recommend setting `max_batch_tokens` from 65536 -> 32768 and `batch_timeout_ms` down from 30 -> 10 for the streaming class. That will reduce padding and expose stalls earlier.

Priya (sre): what's risk of latched throughput drop if we lower max_batch_tokens? any customer QPS that will fall below acceptable?

Maya (observability): throughput hit should be ~5-8% for stdout generation workloads, latency p99 should drop to ~900ms in the test cluster. I'll run a canary sim on scale.

Ava (oncall): I'll run the changes in this order: 1) quick config change to reduce `max_batch_tokens` and `batch_timeout_ms` on cont-batch route for streaming; 2) enable seqlen bucketing; 3) enable preemptive scheduling if the first two don't fully resolve. I'll document and get approvals.

Jules (backend): new config diff (ready for hot reload):
```
# cont-batch policy override for streaming route
cont_batch.streaming.max_batch_tokens = 32768
cont_batch.streaming.batch_timeout_ms = 10
cont_batch.streaming.enable_seqlen_bucketing = true
cont_batch.streaming.bucket_threshold = 1024
cont_batch.streaming.preemptive_priority = "streaming"
```

Ava (oncall): applying step 1 now (hot-reload config) — will monitor.

incident-bot: ACTION: hotpatch config applied by Ava at 3109876620.

Maya (observability): dashboards updating — initial sign: p99 down from 2.8s -> 1.1s across affected hosts, streaming stalls rate halved. tail queue length decreasing.

Liam (customer-ops): any customers we should proactively notify? I can draft a message if there are user-facing errors.

Priya (sre): confirm root-cause still likely mixed sequence-length amplification plus scheduler fairness. If p99 stays under 1.5s we can avoid a full incident notification but keep customers informed.

Jules (backend): recommend follow-up: (A) adopt permanent seqlen bucketing in prod, (B) add dynamic batch sizing that caps token padding ratio, (C) improve scheduler fairness metrics with per-seqlen priority. I'll open tracking tickets.

Ava (oncall): running step 2 (enable seqlen bucketing cluster-wide). Hot-reload coming up.

incident-bot: NOTICE: config-hot-reload started by Ava at 3109876685.

Ben (infra): host kernel delays still present on a couple of nodes — I'm isolating noisy tenant and moving pods off two affected GPU hosts.

Maya (observability): after bucketing p99 ~0.78s, p95 ~95ms. streaming_disconnects dropped to baseline. Good signal across us-west-2.

Liam (customer-ops): sending note to impacted customers in the morning window: short degradation, mitigated, no persistent errors now. Will include root-cause as "batching amplification due to mixed sequence lengths; mitigated via temporary batch size limits and sequence-length bucketing."

Priya (sre): please add a follow-up action to run load tests with long-tail sequence distribution (10% > 2k tokens) to validate new defaults.

Jules (backend): ticket created: RED-1234 "cont-batch: seqlen-bucketing + dynamic-batch-sizing" with proposed rollout plan and perf targets.

Ava (oncall): status: mitigation applied, monitoring green for 18m, p99 below SLO. oncall handoff at 04:30UTC today to Priya. Leaving notes in pager duty.

Priya (sre): taking handoff. if any regression ping me and we'll escalate.

Ava (oncall): handoff ack. final notes: root cause = padding amplification in cont-batch scheduler due to mixed sequence-length grouping; mitigations applied: reduced max_batch_tokens, lowered batch_timeout_ms for streaming class, enabled seqlen bucketing; next steps: implement dynamic batch token cap, add preemptive scheduling and long-tail load tests.

Maya (observability): saving graphs + alert runbook to the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/RED-3125 (will attach timeline).

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated - monitoring continues. handoff completed.

Priya (sre): thanks team. closing paging loop for now. :thumbsup:

Ava (oncall): good job all.
